title: Why a Hotter Pan Can Make Water Last Longer
description:
Why can a hotter pan make a drop of water last longer?

Rapid vapor formation beneath the drop creates a cushion, reducing direct liquid–metal contact. Heat still crosses that gas layer, but less direct contact can let the drop persist longer.

This is conditional: the surface and drop matter, and more heat above the transition can increase evaporation again.

Original qualitative illustration with synthetic narration; vapor gap enlarged. Sources: Dupeux et al. (2014), Lyu et al. (2019), and the Leidenfrost compilation hosted by Reed College.
#LeidenfrostEffect #Physics
firstComment: Hotter is not an always-rule. Surface and drop conditions matter, and extra heat above the transition can increase evaporation again. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6499590/
